verdict.rationale: Jitsu's MCP docs say an approved agent client receives a "scoped, revocable token" through an OAuth 2.1 browser flow. The changelog also lists named user API tokens with expiration. However, nothing documents what the scopes are or whether a user can pick least-privilege permissions, and the headless fallback is a personal API key with no stated scoping. missing for 10: documented scope/permission model (e.g., read-only or per-resource scopes), user-selectable least-privilege scopes for agent tokens, scoping for headless personal API keys, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Approve it once and the client gets a scoped, revocable token.
For interactive clients, authentication is OAuth 2.1 — you don't paste an API key.
named user API tokens with expiration
